facts.statement: The genus Ajkaceratops was described in 2010.
facts.quote: Ajkaceratops (pronounced "oi-ka-sera-tops") is a genus of ceratopsian dinosaur described in 2010.

facts.statement: Ajkaceratops lived during the Late Cretaceous in the western Tethyan archipelago, which is now part of Europe.
facts.quote: It lived during the Late Cretaceous in the western Tethyan archipelago, in what is now Europe.

facts.statement: The genus name Ajkaceratops honors the Hungarian town of Ajka where the fossils were found and the Greek word for "horned face".
facts.quote: The generic name, Ajkaceratops, honors Ajka, a town in Hungary where the fossils were first discovered, combined with the given greek nomination ceratops, meaning "horned face".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MTM V2009.192.1 consists of a few skull fragments including the snout, fused premaxillae, and maxillae fragments.
facts.quote: The holotype, cataloged as MTM V2009.192.1, consists only of a few skull fragments, including snout with proposed rostral bone, fused premaxillae, and maxillae fragments (beak and jaw fragments).

facts.statement: The Ajkaceratops fossils are housed in the Hungarian Natural History Museum in Budapest.
facts.quote: These fossils are kept in the Hungarian Natural History Museum, in Budapest.

facts.statement: Based on fragmentary fossils, Ajkaceratops was estimated to have a body length of 1 meter.
facts.quote: Although the fossils are fragmentary, the paper describing Ajkaceratops estimated a body length of 1 m.

facts.statement: Ajkaceratops masticated food in a circular motion.
facts.quote: Ajkaceratops masticated circumpalinally.

facts.statement: Ajkaceratops lived during the Santonian stage, approximately 86 to 84 million years ago.
facts.quote: This strata dates to the Santonian stage, around 86 to 84 million years ago.

facts.statement: Ajkaceratops fossils were found in the Csehbánya Formation, interpreted as a floodplain and channel deposit made of clay, silt, sand, and sandstone.
facts.quote: The fossils of Ajkaceratops were discovered in the Csehbánya Formation, which is interpreted as a floodplain and channel deposit formed by variegated clay, silt with interbedded grey and brown sand, and sandstone beds.

facts.statement: When first described, Ajkaceratops was considered most similar to the Asian protoceratopsid Bagaceratops.
facts.quote: When first described, the fossils were stated to most closely resemble those of the Asian protoceratopsid Bagaceratops.

facts.statement: Later research questioned Ajkaceratops's classification as a ceratopsian because its proposed rostral bone has a sub-circular cross-section and pitted texture unlike other ceratopsians.
facts.quote: However, later research questioned this referral. The proposed rostral bone of Ajkaceratops differs markedly from the rostral morphology of other ceratopsians, possessing a sub-circular cross-section, pitted texture instead of grooves, and a lack of lateral slicing edges.

facts.statement: In 2026, a more complete skull specimen supported the classification of Ajkaceratops as a ceratopsian.
facts.quote: In 2026, Susannah Maidment and colleagues described MTM 2025.1.1, a new specimen referable to Ajkaceratops from the type locality in the Csehbánya Formation, comprising a much more complete skull. Using these new remains, the authors supported a position for this genus as a ceratopsian.

facts.statement: Ajkaceratops fossils represent the first discovery of this dinosaur group in Europe.
facts.quote: Ésta sería la primera vez que se encontraron fósiles de este grupo en Europa.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Ajkaceratops is a unique ceratopsian or an enigmatic ornithischian with uncertain affinities.
facts.quote: Aunque aún sigue existiendo la posibilidad de que Ajkaceratops sea un ceratopsio bastante peculiar, también puede tratarse de un ornitisquio enigmático de afinidades inciertas.

facts.statement: Some studies based on the premaxilla reinterpretation suggest Ajkaceratops is a basal ornithopod, specifically the sister taxon to Changmiania.
facts.quote: En una redescripción de la anatomía craneana del neornitisquio Jeholosaurus del Cretácico Inferior, Bertozzo et al. pusieron a prueba la posición filogenética de Ajkaceratops con base en la interpretación del premaxilar y encontraron que era el taxón hermano de Changmiania, implicando que era en realidad un ornitópodo basal.

facts.statement: Fossils of Ajkaceratops were discovered in the Csehbánya Formation.
facts.quote: Los fósiles de Ajkaceratops fueron descubiertos en la Formación Csehbánya

facts.statement: Ajkaceratops shared its environment with Rhabdodon, nodosaurids, non-avian theropods, enantiornithine birds, eusuchian crocodilians, azhdarchid pterosaurs, Bothremydidae turtles, and teiid lizards.
facts.quote: Ajkaceratops compartió su entorno con otros dinosaurios como Rhabdodon, nodosáuridos, terópodos no aviares, y aves enatiornites así como cocodrilos eusuquianos, pterosaurios azdárquidos, tortugas de la familia Bothremydidae, y lagartos teíidos

facts.statement: Ajkaceratops belongs to the parent group Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: Parent group: Ceratopsia

facts.statement: Ajkaceratops is classified in the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: The time range for Ajkaceratops is the Santonian, from 85.7 to 83.6 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Santonian (85.7 to 83.6 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is one recorded fossil occurrence of Ajkaceratops in the Paleobiology Database.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1

facts.statement: New remains of Ajkaceratops kozmai were found in the Late Cretaceous Csehbánya Formation in Hungary, according to Maidment et al. (2026).
facts.quote: Maidment et al. (2026) use new remains of Ajkaceratops kozmai from the Late Cretaceous Csehbánya Formation (Hungary)
